verdict.rationale: Name.com's own API documents DNS zone management: you can create records by specifying type (e.g. A, MX, CNAME), host, value and TTL, and list all records for a domain. That establishes bundled DNS hosting with configurable TTLs, but the evidence doesn't show full record-type breadth, minimum TTLs, or a developer-friendly management UI, and one community user would steer people elsewhere for DNS hosting. missing for 10: documented list of all supported record types (e.g. CAA, SRV, TXT, ALIAS), stated minimum/low TTL values, DNS management UI documentation or hands-on corroboration, independent confirmation of DNS hosting quality

support.subject: As a developer, full DNS hosting comes with the domain — every record type, low TTLs, and a management UI that doesn't fight me

citations.quote: Adds a new DNS record to the specified domain zone. Provide the record type (e.g. A, MX, CNAME), host, value, and TTL.
Lists all DNS records for a specified domain.
